name: CI
on:
  - push
  - pull_request
jobs:
  test:
    name: Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version:
          - 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
      - name: Enable pnpm
        run: corepack enable pnpm
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Run tests
        run: pnpm run test

{
  "name": "test",
  "private": true,
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "engines": {
    "node": ">= 16.0.0"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "eslint-check": "eslint --max-warnings=0 .",
    "prettier-check": "prettier --check .",
    "type-check": "tsc --noEmit",
    "test": "tap --ts suite/"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/node-fetch": "2.6.2",
    "@types/sinon": "10.0.13",
    "@types/tap": "15.0.7",
    "@vercel/style-guide": "3.0.0",

# External API call example

## How to use

Download the example [or clone the repo](https://github.com/vercel/micro):

```bash
curl https://codeload.github.com/vercel/micro/tar.gz/master | tar -xz --strip=2 micro-master/examples/external-api-call
cd external-api-call
```

Install it and run:

```bash
npm install
npm run start
```

## The idea behind the example

Shows how to get data from an external api using async/await.

name: Release

# On every push to main, changesets/action either opens a "Version Packages"
# pull request from the pending changesets, or publishes to npm when that pull
# request is merged.
#
# Publishing uses npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC) with provenance, so there is no
# npm token. The Trusted Publisher of `micro` on npmjs.com must use:
#   Repository: vercel/micro
#   Workflow:   release.yml
# npm binds the Trusted Publisher to this file name: renaming this file breaks
# publishing until the npm configuration is updated.
#
# changesets/action pushes the release commit and the tags through the GitHub
# API, so GitHub signs them.
#
# Run this workflow manually on main to retry a failed publish. The 9.x branch
# has its own release.yml, which publishes canary versions: run it manually on
# 9.x.
#
# See https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}

jobs:
  release:
    name: Release
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0

      - name: Setup pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@fc06bc1257f339d1d5d8b3a19a8cae5388b55320 # v4.4.0

      # Node 24 ships an npm version that can authenticate the publish with OIDC.
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
          registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Create release pull request or publish to npm
        uses: changesets/action@198f833dd7d863100ea6e28967bc9a9fdefadb0a # v2.1.0
        with:
          publish-script: pnpm release
        env:
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: 'true'

# GraphQL Request example

## How to use

Download the example [or clone the repo](https://github.com/vercel/micro):

```bash
curl https://codeload.github.com/vercel/micro/tar.gz/master | tar -xz --strip=2 micro-master/examples/with-graphql-request
cd with-graphql-request
```

Install it and run:

```bash
$ yarn install # (or `$ npm install`)
$ yarn run start # (or `$ npm run start`)
```

## The idea behind the example

Shows how to get data from a GraphQL endpoint using [GraphQL Request](https://github.com/graphcool/graphql-request).
This example relies on [graph.cool](https://www.graph.cool) for its GraphQL backend.
